intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that isolated glycolic aciduria (GYCA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HAO1 gene (605023), which encodes glycolate oxidase, on chromosome 20p12.

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria (GYCA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the HAO1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Direct DNA sequencing of glycolate oxidase gene (HAO1) revealed a homozygous c.814-1G>C mutation in the invariant -1 position of intron 5 splice acceptor site.
checks.explanation: Homozygous HAO1 splice mutation identified as the cause of isolated glycolic aciduria.

checks.claim: The HAO1 gene encodes glycolate oxidase.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in HAO1 encoding glycolate oxidase cause isolated glycolic aciduria.
checks.explanation: The title states that HAO1 encodes glycolate oxidase.

checks.claim: The HAO1 gene is located on chromosome 20p12.
checks.evidence_quote: Direct DNA sequencing of glycolate oxidase gene (HAO1)
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene named in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Isolated glycolic aciduria is an autosomal recessive metabolic condition caused by deficiency of glycolate oxidase, the peroxisomal liver enzyme that oxidizes glycolate to glyoxylate. Affected individuals excrete large amounts of glycolate in the urine. Oxalate excretion is normal, so they do not develop the hyperoxaluria, nephrocalcinosis or kidney stones seen in primary hyperoxaluria. The condition seems to be clinically benign. This observation supports pharmacologic inhibition of glycolate oxidase as a substrate-reduction treatment for primary hyperoxaluria.

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria is an autosomal recessive metabolic condition.
checks.evidence_quote: Two brothers, born to consanguineous healthy parents of Arab descent
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by healthy consanguineous parents and a homozygous mutation, but the abstract does not state it for isolated glycolic aciduria.

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria is caused by deficiency of glycolate oxidase.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results pinpoint the expression of defective splice variant of glycolate oxidase as the cause of isolated asymptomatic glycolic aciduria.
checks.explanation: The abstract identifies defective glycolate oxidase as the cause.

checks.claim: Glycolate oxidase is a peroxisomal liver enzyme that oxidizes glycolate to glyoxylate.
checks.evidence_quote: glyoxylate, the product of glycolate oxidation, and the immediate precursor of oxalate
checks.explanation: The abstract says the enzyme is liver-specific and that glyoxylate is the product of glycolate oxidation. It does not say the enzyme is peroxisomal.

checks.claim: Individuals with isolated glycolic aciduria excrete large amounts of glycolate in the urine.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband showed markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion
checks.explanation: The abstract reports markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion.

checks.claim: Oxalate excretion is normal in individuals with isolated glycolic aciduria.
checks.evidence_quote: with normal excretion of oxalate, citrate and glycerate
checks.explanation: The abstract reports normal oxalate excretion.

checks.claim: Individuals with isolated glycolic aciduria do not develop the hyperoxaluria, nephrocalcinosis or kidney stones seen in primary hyperoxaluria.
checks.evidence_quote: Abdominal ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys with normal echotexture.
checks.explanation: Normal oxalate excretion and normal kidneys on ultrasound are reported. Nephrocalcinosis and stones are not mentioned.

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria seems to be clinically benign.
checks.evidence_quote: the cause of isolated asymptomatic glycolic aciduria
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the condition as asymptomatic.

checks.claim: The benign nature of isolated glycolic aciduria supports pharmacologic inhibition of glycolate oxidase as a substrate-reduction treatment for primary hyperoxaluria.
checks.evidence_quote: Targeting HAO1 to reduce substrate for oxalate production in the liver is one potential therapeutic approach.
checks.explanation: The paper also says 'our data support the potential safety of HAO1 inhibition as a chronic therapy for the devastating metabolic disease PH1'.

paragraphs.text: Frishberg et al. (2014) reported a child with markedly increased urinary glycolate excretion and normal urinary oxalate excretion. The child had no evidence of the renal stone disease or nephrocalcinosis seen in primary hyperoxaluria.

checks.claim: Frishberg et al. (2014) reported a child with markedly increased urinary glycolate excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband showed markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion
checks.explanation: The proband, one of two brothers evaluated for psychomotor delay, had markedly increased glycolic acid excretion.

checks.claim: The child with glycolic aciduria reported by Frishberg et al. (2014) had normal urinary oxalate excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: with normal excretion of oxalate, citrate and glycerate
checks.explanation: The abstract reports normal oxalate excretion in the proband.

checks.claim: The child with glycolic aciduria reported by Frishberg et al. (2014) had no evidence of renal stone disease or nephrocalcinosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Abdominal ultrasound showed normal-sized kidneys with normal echotexture.
checks.explanation: Ultrasound was normal, but stones and nephrocalcinosis are not explicitly mentioned.

paragraphs.text: McGregor et al. (2020) described a healthy adult with complete loss of HAO1 function. This person had raised plasma and urinary glycolate but normal oxalate levels and no apparent clinical abnormality. The authors presented the case as human evidence that long-term glycolate oxidase inhibition would be safe as a treatment for primary hyperoxaluria.

checks.claim: McGregor et al. (2020) described a healthy adult with complete loss of HAO1 function.
checks.evidence_quote: A healthy adult woman with complete lifelong germline knockout of HAO1 (hydroxyacid oxidase 1, encoding glycolate oxidase) was identified.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: The adult with complete loss of HAO1 function described by McGregor et al. (2020) had raised plasma glycolate levels.
checks.evidence_quote: her plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate levels were markedly elevated
checks.explanation: Plasma glycolate was 171 nmol/mL against a reference of ≤14.

checks.claim: The adult with complete loss of HAO1 function described by McGregor et al. (2020) had raised urinary glycolate levels.
checks.evidence_quote: her plasma glycolate and urinary glycolate levels were markedly elevated
checks.explanation: Urinary glycolate was six times the upper limit of normal.

checks.claim: The adult with complete loss of HAO1 function described by McGregor et al. (2020) had normal oxalate levels.
checks.evidence_quote: plasma and urinary oxalate were both normal
checks.explanation: Both plasma and urinary oxalate were normal.

checks.claim: The adult with complete loss of HAO1 function described by McGregor et al. (2020) had no apparent clinical abnormality.
checks.evidence_quote: In this woman, lifelong HAO1 knockout is safe and without clinical phenotype
checks.explanation: The paper states she had no clinical phenotype.

checks.claim: McGregor et al. (2020) presented the HAO1-deficient adult as human evidence that long-term glycolate oxidase inhibition would be safe as a treatment for primary hyperoxaluria.
checks.evidence_quote: Most importantly, our data support the potential safety of HAO1 inhibition as a chronic therapy for the devastating metabolic disease PH1.
checks.explanation: The authors present her case as evidence for the safety of long-term inhibition.

paragraphs.text: The biochemical hallmark of the condition is glycolic aciduria with normal oxalate excretion. This pattern is consistent with a block in the conversion of glycolate to glyoxylate, the immediate precursor of oxalate (Frishberg et al., 2014).

checks.claim: The biochemical hallmark of isolated glycolic aciduria is glycolic aciduria with normal oxalate excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: The proband showed markedly increased urinary glycolic acid excretion with normal excretion of oxalate, citrate and glycerate.
checks.explanation: The finding is reported for the proband. The abstract uses 'hallmark' only for glycolic aciduria with hyperoxaluria in PH1, not for this condition.

checks.claim: The pattern of glycolic aciduria with normal oxalate excretion is consistent with a block in the conversion of glycolate to glyoxylate.
checks.evidence_quote: glyoxylate, the product of glycolate oxidation, and the immediate precursor of oxalate
checks.explanation: The block in conversion follows from glycolate oxidase deficiency but is not stated explicitly as an interpretation.

checks.claim: Glyoxylate is the immediate precursor of oxalate.
checks.evidence_quote: glyoxylate, the product of glycolate oxidation, and the immediate precursor of oxalate
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Isolated glycolic aciduria follows autosomal recessive inheritance. The reported affected individuals were homozygous for mutations in the HAO1 gene (Frishberg et al., 2014; McGregor et al., 2020).

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria follows autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Two brothers, born to consanguineous healthy parents of Arab descent
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied by consanguinity and homozygosity but is not explicitly stated for this condition.

checks.claim: The reported individuals with isolated glycolic aciduria were homozygous for mutations in the HAO1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed a homozygous c.814-1G>C mutation in the invariant -1 position of intron 5 splice acceptor site
checks.explanation: The mutation was homozygous in this paper's family.

paragraphs.text: In a child with isolated glycolic aciduria, Frishberg et al. (2014) identified a homozygous mutation in the HAO1 gene.

checks.claim: Frishberg et al. (2014) identified a homozygous mutation in the HAO1 gene in a child with isolated glycolic aciduria.
checks.evidence_quote: Direct DNA sequencing of glycolate oxidase gene (HAO1) revealed a homozygous c.814-1G>C mutation
checks.explanation: A homozygous HAO1 mutation was identified.

paragraphs.text: McGregor et al. (2020) used genetic data from a population cohort to identify a healthy adult who was homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in the HAO1 gene.

checks.claim: McGregor et al. (2020) used genetic data from a population cohort to identify a healthy adult who was homozygous for a loss-of-function variant in the HAO1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We exome sequenced two large population-based cohorts with substantial autozygosity (Born In Bradford, Genes and Health [Narasimhan et al., 2016; Finer, 2018]). A healthy adult woman with complete lifelong germline knockout of HAO1
checks.explanation: The cohort sequencing, the healthy adult and the homozygous loss-of-function variant are all reported.

paragraphs.text: Because humans lacking glycolate oxidase appear healthy, the condition has served as a natural model supporting glycolate oxidase inhibition (for example, by RNA interference targeting HAO1) as a treatment for primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (McGregor et al., 2020).

checks.claim: Humans lacking glycolate oxidase appear healthy.
checks.evidence_quote: In this woman, lifelong HAO1 knockout is safe and without clinical phenotype
checks.explanation: This is based on a single individual. The paper cautions that effects in other genetic backgrounds could not be evaluated, and the earlier reported children had complicating factors.

checks.claim: Isolated glycolic aciduria has served as a natural model supporting glycolate oxidase inhibition as a treatment for primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
checks.evidence_quote: This case demonstrates the value of studying the lifelong complete knockdown of a target protein in a living human to aid development of a potential therapeutic, both in de-risking the approach
checks.explanation: The paper presents the human knockout as a natural model that de-risks HAO1 inhibition for PH1.

checks.claim: RNA interference targeting HAO1 is an example of glycolate oxidase inhibition as a treatment for primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
checks.evidence_quote: HAO1 (glycolate oxidase) silencing is the mechanism of lumasiran, an investigational RNA interference therapeutic for primary hyperoxaluria type 1.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

references.citation: Frishberg Y, Zeharia A, Lyakhovetsky R, Bargal R, Belostotsky R. Mutations in HAO1 encoding glycolate oxidase cause isolated glycolic aciduria. J Med Genet 51: 526-9, 2014. [PubMed: 24996905]
